answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when an independent audit proves fraud. Auditors sample completed work and compare it with hidden test cases; repeated failures disable the account and route its remaining stake to affected users. A sybil can still create many names, but every name needs capital and each risky attempt can burn it, so multiplying identities raises the attacker’s cost rather than multiplying influence for free. A harbor, falcon, or walnut label does not change that accounting.
